verdict: Assembly direction and the behaviour-preserving refactor hold up, but the scale test measures code defaults rather than the shipped rules and skips the new-year turn, so the 287 ms figure says little about the real game. At target scale the shipped merchant settings (bids=2, judge_hops=3) and the yearly contract and investment scans are the real performance risk, and banks are the cheapest current win. No timings here were measured, because Unity was off limits: all cost figures are estimates from reading the code.

other EditMode tests: a scripted scan for assertions and keyword greps only, not read by hand

findings.title: Shipped bid and look-ahead settings make each stationary merchant walk every unstocked cell with a recursive route search
findings.evidence: config.csv sets merchants.judge_hops,3 and merchants.bids,2. TryStartTrip then always calls BidForWhatIsMissing, which loops `for (int cell = MarketCellStart[node]; ...) { if (Stock[cell] > 0) continue;`: the complement of the stocked-cell list that ListStockedCells built because 'most cells have no stock'. Each such cell runs WeighBid over all routes, and WeighUnit calls Beyond, which recurses JudgeHops-1 levels with a FindCell binary search per edge.
findings.failure_scenario: Full-scale map with the shipped merchant settings: a region market has about 4,000 cells and few are stocked (FullScale makes about 55 goods). One region group does about 4,000 cells x 6 routes x roughly 6 FindCell calls = about 144,000 binary searches; 400 region groups and 1,500 city groups (shipped counts, config.csv:77-78) reach the order of 10^8 searches per turn before allowing for groups on the road. That estimates to seconds per turn even under Burst, against 110 ms for the merchants step today. core.absorb and fit, range and cash checks would reduce this, so the exact factor needs a run.
findings.fix: First measure: FullScale plus these two config lines. Smallest cut that keeps the rule: per node and turn, list unstocked cells that any route could profit from once, before the per-group loop, and memoise Beyond per (from, to, good, hops) for groups with the same reach and vehicle. Behaviour must stay byte-identical under GoldenRunTests.

findings.title: The scale test measures code defaults, skips the new-year turn and has no time limit, so it cannot catch a slowdown of the shipped game
findings.evidence: FullScale() adds no config.csv, so defaults apply: judge hops 1 (shipped 3), bids off (shipped 2), trip costs off (shipped 1), InvestmentPaybackYears 0 and ContractsPerNation 0, both of which switch their systems off (shipped 8 and 8). The settled window is turns 60 to 72, which holds no new-year turn (52, 104), so yearly systems do not run in it. The only assertions are `Assert.AreEqual(1580, markets.MarketCount)` and the good count; time is only logged. The guide says 'still within budget' but states no number, and 00_Architecture.md:138 still quotes 33.6 ms/turn against the 287 ms in 04_Roadmap.md.
findings.failure_scenario: A change that makes the new-year turn take 10 s, or makes shipped-config merchant turns 20 times slower, passes the scale test and leaves its logged figure unchanged. It also runs 9,250 groups where the shipped config gives 4,460 on the same map, so the figure matches neither configuration the owner might mean.
findings.fix: Build FullScale with the sample config.csv (dropping only map-specific lines), log the worst turn including a new-year turn, and assert a written per-turn budget that the guide and 00_Architecture.md quote.

findings.title: agents.banks is quadratic: every broke merchant without a loan scans the whole cargo table each week
findings.evidence: LendToNpcs: `long limit = config.LoanToValue.MulInt(_sheet.CargoValue(CargoHolders.Merchant(new AgentId(a)), node));`. CargoValue calls CargoTable.Collect, which tests all rows, and each `r < Count` goes through List and interface dispatch in NativeTable.Count. A group with no cargo gets limit 0, Lend returns 0, no loan row is added, and it scans again next week. The value is computed even when Lend would refuse anyway because of a credit crunch or an empty reserve.
findings.failure_scenario: About 9,000 cargo rows and several hundred negative-cash groups without loans give millions of row tests per turn through managed indexers. About 500 such groups at roughly 270 us per scan (an Editor estimate) would account for the 144 ms; the actual count of such groups was not measured.
findings.fix: Cheapest cut, no rule change: before the agent loop, make one pass over the cargo rows summing quantity x price per merchant into a scratch long[] (the sum does not depend on order), and read it in the loop. O(agents + rows). Also read Count into a local in Collect, and skip the valuation when Lend cannot lend. GoldenRunTests must stay unchanged.

findings.title: New-year contract signing and investment rescan whole tables per node, giving a yearly freeze the scale test never sees
findings.evidence: Each Sign call recomputes WidestGap from nothing: every sufficiently stocked cell of the nation x every node of the nation x TryFindCell, up to contract.per_nation (8) times for each nation. Invest loops `for (int f = 0; f < _facilities.Count; f++) { if (_facilities.Node[f] != node) continue;` and RichestAt loops all groups, for each node, up to InvestmentProjectsPerNode (2) times. All of this is managed code on the main thread.
findings.failure_scenario: At full scale: 25 nations x 8 signs x (47,000 cells x assumed 10% above min stock x 62 nodes) is about 58 million binary searches, plus about 1,580 x 2 x 8,500 = 27 million facility tests. Estimated at seconds in the Editor and worse on Android, on the same turn as a dozen other yearly systems, so the game hitches once per in-game year. The 10% share is an assumption.
findings.fix: Investment: build a node-to-facility list once at the start of the yearly pass. Contracts: compute the candidate gaps once per nation, sort them, and take the top ones while skipping contracted or refused pairs, instead of rescanning for each of the 8 signs. Check tie order against the golden hashes.

findings.title: Agents.merchants at 110 ms repeats the same per-node lookups for every group
findings.evidence: WeighCell runs WeighRoute for each stocked cell and route: MayGo (which climbs parents in Within) and FindCell (binary search of the destination), then WeighUnit. The destination cell depends only on (route, good), and MayGo's answer for a group does not change between cells, yet both are recomputed. HoldsLicenses rehashes `DetRandom.For(Seed, 0, LicenseStream, a)` although it depends only on the group id. The job is single-threaded (`job.Schedule().Complete()`, ArbitrageMerchantBehavior.cs:234), since order is part of the result.
findings.failure_scenario: Default config, full scale: about 55 stocked cells x 6 routes = about 330 route evaluations per acting upper-level group. With about 4,000 acting groups (assumed) that is 1.3 million evaluations, which at about 50 ns with Editor safety checks gives about 65 ms, a large part of the logged 110 ms. Editor safety checks inflate this compared with a player build, so the real share needs a profile.
findings.fix: Inside ListStockedCells, store the destination cell for each (stocked cell, route) so each group reads it instead of searching; compute per-route MayGo once in NewSearch; precompute HoldsLicenses per group at Initialize. These change no result, so golden hashes stay put.

findings.title: The presentation boundary holds only because no UI exists: most of SimulationView cannot be called from FES.Unity
findings.evidence: FES.Unity references only FES.Core, FES.Data and FES.Simulation, but the view's signatures use FES.Agents types (TripQuote, CargoItem, LoanInfo, AuctionInfo, LicenseInfo) and GroupInfo exposes GroupKind. Separately, `public WorldState World`, `public readonly SimContext Context` and `SimulationView.Database` are public, and SimulationConfig has public mutable fields; SimulationTests.cs:551 sets `sim.Database.Config.LodMode = 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: The first cart screen calling `view.GetCart(list)` fails to compile with CS0012 until FES.Agents is referenced. Once it is, `Simulation.World.Get<BankState>().Reserve[0] = 0` also compiles from UI code. Even today `view.Database.Config.LodMode = 0` changes the rules from presentation, contrary to 'UI code cannot change simulation state' (SimulationView.cs:148-150).
findings.fix: Decide before building UI: either move the DTOs and enums the view returns into FES.Core or FES.Simulation, or accept a reference to FES.Agents and say so in the guide. Expose World and Context to tests through InternalsVisibleTo, and hand presentation a read-only config view.

findings.title: The Extension Guide promises adding features without editing systems, but real features edit about two dozen files
findings.evidence: Pipeline.cs: 'no existing system needs to change'. Commit e1930cb (credit, sea trade, market package) touched 25 production files with 1,862 insertions, including MerchantJob +457, MadeToOrder +217, ArbitrageMerchantBehavior +125; 5dbb474 and 4ad3912 touched 20 each. Some of those edits are rule changes rather than plain additions. One merchant rule needs a config field, a reader line, a config.csv row, a job field (the job has 126) and an assignment in SetRules, SetPlaces, SetTraits or SetGroups. A new money holder must also be added by hand to MoneyLedger.ContinentMoney and MoneyTotals. Systems share state through public arrays reached by `world.Get<T>()`, including from static helpers in MoneyLedger.
findings.failure_scenario: A new merchant rule follows the guide, adds a value field to the job and forgets its assignment: the field is silently 0 and nothing fails to compile, so the rule is quietly off. A new holder of coins that misses ContinentMoney is caught only if a conservation test happens to run the path.
findings.fix: Correct the guide so it states the real cost and lists the merchant-rule checklist. For the job, pass the value settings in one struct built in one place, so a missing rule cannot be missed by splitting across four setters.

findings.title: Golden runs never borrow or issue commands, and no test asserts ship, cart or warehouse seizure, though the refactor moved that code
findings.evidence: StateHash only calls `sim.AdvanceTurn()`, so a golden run has no player loan and can never reach Seize. In the tests, CollateralKind.Ship, CartCargo and WarehouseCargo have zero mentions; only Deposit and Facility are asserted. `HedgePaid` (ClaimCover's payout), `SupplyContractBroken` and `LostWithGroups` also have zero mentions. Commit 485b660 split Seize into SeizeDeposits, SeizeStoredCargo, SeizeCart, SeizeShip and SeizeFacilities. Reading that diff found no change in behaviour, but no automated check confirms it. The standards doc does disclose that golden runs omit commands.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit makes SeizeShip charge the wrong continent's coin or skip Repay. Every golden hash and all listed bank tests still pass, and the loan book or the coin total goes wrong only for a player who defaults while owning a ship.
findings.fix: Add one scripted golden run that issues a fixed command list (loan, ship, cargo in cart and warehouse, default, auction, save and load), plus direct tests for each seizure kind and for a price-cover payout.

findings.title: View.CreditLimit is quadratic in cargo rows and allocates on every read
findings.evidence: CollectHolders: `if (!into.Contains(Holder[r])) into.Add(Holder[r]);` with one holder per merchant group, used only to find guild halls. `public long CreditLimit => new PlayerBalanceSheet(_world, Database).CreditLimit(...)` allocates the sheet and two lists and does about a dozen dictionary lookups per read. Cargo.cs:163 still says linear search is 'fine while only the player's cart holds cargo', which stopped being true when merchants began carrying goods.
findings.failure_scenario: A bank screen showing the credit limit every frame at full scale: about 9,000 holders means about 40 million comparisons per read, plus a full table scan per player facility and GC allocation, so the frame rate collapses on Android while the screen is open. The guide promises views that avoid per-frame allocations (01_Extension_Guide.md:72).
findings.fix: Have CargoTable expose only guild-hall holders by filtering in one pass with no Contains, keep one cached PlayerBalanceSheet in SimulationView, and cache the value per turn.

findings.title: SimulationRunner runs a full turn and hashes all saved state synchronously on the main thread
findings.evidence: `Simulation.AdvanceTurn();` then a Debug.Log containing `Simulation.ComputeHash()`, which serialises every persistent component byte by byte through an FNV stream. The Build call in Start is also synchronous, including the 25-million-step route search in FindWaysToward (ArbitrageMerchantBehavior.cs:186-195). This is the only presentation code there is, and it has no turn scheduling, no save or load entry and no error path.
findings.failure_scenario: On Android at full scale, each Advance Turn blocks the frame for at least the 287 ms Editor figure (the device figure was never measured, per 00_Architecture.md:139) plus a full-state hash. If the data fails validation, the exception ends the coroutine and IsReady stays false with no user-visible state.
findings.fix: Keep the hash behind a debug flag. Before real UI, split a turn's work across frames or run it off the main thread with reads only between turns, as GameSimulation's thread note already requires. Catch and surface Build errors.

findings.title: Merchant trip statistics use magic array indices, and the job's setup was split into arbitrary groups
findings.evidence: `_tripStats = new NativeArray<long>(21, ...)`, written as `TripStats[13] += premium` and mapped by position to `stats.SpentCover += _tripStats[13]`. The 127 assignments were split into SetRules, SetPlaces, SetTraits and SetGroups to satisfy the 80-line limit: SetTraits also sets MustAct, HedgeRoom, AgentHedge and TripStats, and SetRules sets International and the bill columns. The complexity score fell but the field count did not.
findings.failure_scenario: A new statistic written to `TripStats[18]` by mistake adds to SpentHedge. Money still balances, so only a wrong figure in a measurement report shows it, and these reports drive balance decisions.
findings.fix: Replace the indices with named constants or a blittable stats struct. If the setter split stays, name the groups for what they hold.

findings.title: SourceMetrics does not measure field-initializer lambdas or case guards, and the unused-method regex misses common declarations
findings.evidence: Members skips any `=` to its statement end: `else if (text == "=") head = _i = StatementEnd(_i) + 1;`. Case() walks to `:` without scoring. The PrivateMethod regex needs the line to start with a modifier or type, and its parameter part is `[^;{}=]*`. Interpolated-string holes are blanked with the string. A scan of production code found no such lambda today, so this is a gap rather than a hidden violation. 05_Refactoring_Standards.md lists only recursion, 'unusual syntax' and name collisions as limits.
findings.failure_scenario: `static readonly Func<int,int> F = x => { /* 200 lines, nesting 8 */ };` scores nothing. `case 1 when a && b || c:` adds no complexity. An unused `static int Old(int a = 0) { ... }` or `[MethodImpl(...)] static int Old() { ... }` is not reported by PrivateMethods_AreAllCalled.
findings.fix: Score initializer lambdas as members, send case guards through Scan, allow `=` in the regex's parameter list and strip leading attributes. Add a SourceMetricsTests case for each.

findings.title: Duplicate check demands 100 tokens inside exactly 10 lines, and its token pattern omits arithmetic operators
findings.evidence: It takes `lines.Skip(k).Take(blockLines)`, compares the exact text, and skips when `Tokens(block).Count < blockTokens`. The published rule is 100 tokens spread over at least 10 lines, not within any 10-line window. `+ - * / % ! & | ^ ~` are not in TokenPattern. An in-memory scan of production code found no exact duplicate meeting Sonar's definition; the largest are 8-9 lines (Groups.cs:304 and MerchantMembership.cs:93, MerchantFlowJob.cs:129 and MerchantJob.cs:780), so nothing is hidden today.
findings.failure_scenario: Two copies of a 40-line block averaging 8 tokens per line are 320 tokens over 40 lines, a clear Sonar duplicate, but no 10-line window reaches 100 tokens, so the test passes.
findings.fix: Hash windows of 100 tokens rather than 10 lines, then require the match to span at least 10 lines, and include all operators in the token count.

findings.title: The checks scan a fixed folder list, and the exemption list is not limited the way the document says
findings.evidence: ProductionFolders and SimulationFolders are literals. 'this list can only shrink' holds only for stale entries: anyone can add one. The key is `File + " " + Method.Name`, so an exemption covers all overloads, and AssertWithin applies it to all five limits rather than the one with a reason.
findings.failure_scenario: A new assembly at Assets/_Game/Trade is silently outside every standards, UnityEngine and determinism check. An exemption granted for one large switch also lifts the nesting and parameter limits for a same-named overload in that file.
findings.fix: Enumerate Assets/_Game/* minus Tests and fail on an unknown folder. Key exemptions by file, method and rule.

findings.title: The determinism test's banned list is substring text that misses common forms
findings.evidence: `string[] banned = { "System.Random", "DateTime.Now", "UnityEngine.Random", "GetHashCode()", "float ", "double " };` and any line containing ToDouble is exempt. A grep of simulation folders found no violation today.
findings.failure_scenario: `(double)a / b`, `float[]`, `List<float>`, `DateTime.UtcNow`, `Environment.TickCount`, `Guid.NewGuid()` and `Math.Sqrt` all pass, so nondeterministic state could enter while the test stays green.
findings.fix: Match on word boundaries for float and double, and add the missing APIs to the list.

findings.title: Several tests pin emergent results of [Draft] data, or assert little
findings.evidence: `Assert.Greater(stats.ForcedTrips, 0)` after 3 simulated years and `Assert.Greater(...SpentHedge, 0)` after 6 years run on the shipped sample config. PriceCover_IsBoughtAndKeepsTheCoinsWhole never checks a payout. SampleWorld_RunsOneYear asserts `Turn == WeeksPerYear`, which can only fail by exception, so it is a smoke test. All this comes from a scripted scan plus reading these tests; the others were not judged one by one.
findings.failure_scenario: Retuning a [Draft] number such as the hedge fee or fall chance so that no group ever buys cover fails a test that is about coin conservation. Conversely, a broken payout in ClaimCover still passes it.
findings.fix: Set up the wanted state directly in a small fixture for rule tests, and keep long emergent runs for conservation only.

findings.title: MarketFlows.AddSupply and AddDemand, the documented single entry point, have no callers at all
findings.evidence: A grep of Assets/_Game including tests finds only the two definitions. Real flows write directly, for example `_markets.Supply[to] = MarketStore.ClampToNonNegativeInt(...)`. The guide says 'never MarketStore directly'. The unused-method test checks private methods only, so it cannot report this.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor who follows the guide uses AddSupply and gets event-scaled flows while every comparable existing trade is unscaled. One who copies Contracts.cs gets the opposite. Whether a flow should be scaled becomes accidental.
findings.fix: State the real rule in the guide (executed trades unscaled, production through its modifier slots) and delete the two methods, or route the flows that should scale through them.

findings.title: MoneyTotals can show stale figures after loading a save with the same turn number
findings.evidence: `if (_computedTurn != world.Get<SimClock>().Turn) Recompute(world);`. MoneyTotals is an IWorldComponent, not saved, and is not an ILoadListener; a grep finds only FinanceSystem.cs:85 and this getter calling it, so Load leaves _computedTurn as it was.
findings.failure_scenario: The player loads a turn-90 save, plays to turn 100 and opens the money screen, which caches totals for turn 100. Loading a different save also at turn 100 then shows the other timeline's NationMoneyTotal and ContinentMoneyTotal until the next turn. Only the display is wrong; simulation state is not.
findings.fix: Reset _computedTurn to -1 on load, through a load listener or by having the view compare a load counter.

findings.title: Some parameter objects in the refactor exist only to pass the parameter limit
findings.evidence: TripCharges has five longs copied field by field into TripQuote and is built at a single call site. Its only effect is to bring the constructor to exactly 7 parameters. TripSearch mixes what a group asks with the best result so far in one 15-field struct passed by ref. By contrast ContractRoute and GroupReach name real concepts. 04_Roadmap.md records merchants rising from 106.3 ms (one run) to 109.7 and 112.2 ms; with one baseline run, noise cannot be separated from a cost of the split.
findings.failure_scenario: No wrong result. The cost is one extra type to keep in sync with TripQuote, and a limit that rewards wrapping parameters over reducing them, which the standards' own smell list warns about as data clumps.
findings.fix: Have Quote assign TripQuote through an object initializer or an exemption with a reason, and split TripSearch into asks and best. Take at least three baseline runs before a hot-path refactor.

findings.title: Golden hashes first appear in the refactoring commit itself, so history cannot show they match the code before it
findings.evidence: `git log` shows GoldenRunTests.cs was first added by 485b660, the same commit as the refactor. 04_Roadmap.md states 'Saved states of all eight golden runs unchanged', which can only rest on a run before the commit that is not in the repository. Nor does any test distinguish a refactoring commit that records new hashes, despite the rule at 05_Refactoring_Standards.md:27.
findings.failure_scenario: If the refactor had changed behaviour before the hashes were recorded, the recorded hashes would pin the changed behaviour and every later run would pass. Reading the merchant, bank, contract and migration diffs found no such change; the statement cannot be confirmed from the repository alone, and this review did not run Unity.
findings.fix: Check out 485b660~1 once with the test file added and compare the eight hashes. For later refactors, commit the golden test first.

strengths: Assembly direction is acyclic and compiler-enforced: Core <- Data <- World <- Economy <- Agents <- Simulation <- Unity, with Persistence depending only on Core (all asmdefs read). No simulation file uses UnityEngine by the ArchitectureTests rule.

Refactor behaviour: compared the old and new merchant job line by line for TryStartTrip, SellHere, Depart, BestCarry, WithinTheBankThere and bids, plus Contracts.Sign, ServiceBonds, Invest, Migration and SiteOnLand, and could not find a changed result, ordering or RNG draw. Not every changed file was read; see coverage.
SimulationConfig split: a scripted comparison found the same 259 config key strings before and after 485b660, so no key was dropped by the move to SimulationConfigReader.
Tests changed in 485b660 (DemandTests, EconomyTests, InvestmentTests) only adapt to new signatures; no assertion was weakened.

Per-turn managed allocation looks low: a grep of array, list and LINQ allocations in Agents and Economy shows nearly all in constructors, Initialize, migrations or yearly paths. ProductionSystem.cs:207 is a small per-turn array. Not measured with a profiler.

SourceMetrics tried with nested types, tuple returns, accessors, indexers, operators and constructors by reading the walker: it handles them, and production has no class with a `where T : new()` constraint, the one header form that would be mistaken for a method.
No exact duplicate meeting Sonar's definition exists in production code today, per an independent in-memory scan.
